description: Declares event flags by name: a flag is one yes/no fact of the story that the save keeps ("this pickup was taken", "this door is open", "this cutscene was seen"). Scripts test and set them with sh.flag_get / sh.flag_set, map data (events, world objects, spawn rules, the paper map) names them the same way, and a save stores the names of the flags that are set. Each entry: "description" says what sets the flag and what it changes; "aliases" are former names that still resolve everywhere (old saves, scripts and mods); "old_save_names" are former names that now name another flag, so they are read only from saves written before the rename. The engine gives every flag its save bit itself (the original layout of the base flags is the "event_flags" list of original_order.json). A mod adds its own flags with a flags.json or flags/*.json of the same shape in its folder (names are then <mod folder>:Name). Paper map marks: each mark of a map page has two flags, one per half (for example the arrows of a passable door and the cross of a locked one); the map screen draws a half while its flag is set (menu/map_screen.json names the two flags of every mark). Events set them when a door is found locked, jammed or passed, or a note marks the map. A completed event whose done flag is one of these may still run again (only exclusive and set-flag events stop).

MapMark_Begin.description: The bit just before the first paper map mark (OldTown page, mark 0 is the next bit). The original event code compares done flags with this bit: from it on, a done flag only marks the map and blocks only exclusive and set-flag events (the engine asks for the paper map mark kind instead). Nothing sets or reads it as a flag.
